**Finding: Compliant** (no redline proposed)

The Agreement contains no most-favoured-nation obligation in either direction, which satisfies the preferred position under rule MFN (no MFN obligation on Customer).

What I checked:
- **Targeted searches** for "most favored"/"favourable", "no less favorable", "lowest", "best price", "discount", "similarly situated", "other customers", "preferred" — all returned nothing.
- **Section 4 (Fees)** — fixed license, maintenance/support fees and taxes, plus an audit right; no benchmarking or price-matching.
- **Exhibit B (Pricing, Revenue Sharing Fees, Payment Terms)** — fixed fee lines and fixed revenue-share percentages with defined carve-outs (Application Management Revenue exclusions, Professional Service/Network fees excluded); no obligation on Corio to extend Commerce One terms offered to third parties.
- **Section 2 (Grant of Rights)** — Sections 2.9 (new products) and 2.10 (geographic expansion) leave future licensing to mutual agreement rather than to third-party-benchmarked terms; no MFN mechanic.
- **Exhibit D (Sales and Marketing Cooperation)** — expressly non-binding cooperation only.

Note for the file: because there is no vendor-granted MFN either, Corio has no contractual right to Commerce One's best pricing. That is not a playbook deviation, but if the commercial team wants pricing protection on renewal or on the Year 2–5 fee tiers in Exhibit B, an MFN running **to Corio** would be welcome under this rule and could be raised as an affirmative ask rather than a defensive redline.
